counting_floor_relations.formula: R >= C, C = |F| / 2n; a determined system needs at least as many independent rows as unknowns
counting_floor_relations.note: moves only with the column count

coverage_threshold_relations.formula: R > C * ln(C) / 3; with m = 3 summands on uniform columns a column is missed with probability e^{-3R/C}
coverage_threshold_relations.note: above the counting floor, so it is what a swept run waits for

rho_reference_S.note: pooled because rho's step count varies about 20% between seed sets

aim_at_least_mentioned_columns.caveat: S is still 1.33x rho: closing the relation count to its floor did not produce a crossover
aim_at_least_mentioned_columns.why: ratio to the counting floor fell from 1.73 to 1.03 and cannot fall below 1.00; the lever is terminal

aim_at_uncovered_columns.why: coverage fell 330 -> 117, a 2.8x move in the tracked number; total fell 1.02x

scan_scratch.why: taking four per-trial allocations out of the scan's hot loop measured 5.46 -> 5.58 adds a summand: no change. Kept as a refactor, not claimed as a gain

walked_probe_in_the_harness.why: a first version of the window measurement drew targets with mul_u64, about 59 chained additions, and divided it over 256 summands instead of 15,744. It invented a fourfold window penalty that would have cut the window round's reported gain from 2.7x to 1.3x. Collection walks; the measurement now walks

window_constant_by_base_and_window.why: 2.31 was the full scan on a 5,248-point base; wider bases and narrower windows cost more, up to 23%. Earlier rows re-priced, none deleted

aimed_scan_adds_per_summand.note: the gather an index scan pays is free at every set size a run actually aims at; only a set of one or two columns, which the least-mention rule never produces, costs more

scan_adds_per_summand.note: depends on BOTH base width and window; 2.31 used by the earlier window round was the full scan on a 5,248-point base and undercharges wider bases by up to 23%

select_adds.source: examples/koblitz_phase_prices.rs, measured at each width, never scaled

aimed_at_least_mentioned.reading: full rank at exactly the counting floor

aimed_at_uncovered.reading: coverage moved 2.8x and the total 1.02x: coverage was never the constraint

swept.pivotless_mentions: six at 0x, two at 1x, one at 2x

diagnosis.method: replay a finished run's banked relations in arrival order; report where coverage completes and where full rank does
diagnosis.reading: a column mentioned once is pinned only if every other column in its row is, so the set worth scanning is the least-mentioned columns, which is a counter rather than an elimination

swept.reading: coverage and rank share the coupon-collector threshold when rows are uniform

falsification.abandon_note: the first aim, at uncovered columns, MET an abandon condition (309 relations > 280) and was abandoned as a lever; the least-mention rule is a different aim and is reported separately rather than as a rescue of the same one
falsification.success_condition: whole-pipeline total adds fall >= 1.3x against the matched swept arm, 32/32 verified, 0 rejected, every column covered, aimed scans priced with their own measured constant

ledger.note: every phase priced; select measured at the width, build one addition per stored pair, scan at the constant for its own base and window, descent and linear algebra converted as above

rows.variant: + aim at uncovered columns (relabelling, not kept)

limitations: One degree. n = 41 only; the diagnosis is expected to hold wherever m = 3 and columns = |F|/2n, but that is not measured here.
The two interpolated rows are marked as such; they interpolate between measured windows at the same base width, never across widths.
The frozen ledger rungs sweep and are unchanged: collection_aim is off by default, so an aimed run's counters are not a swept run's.
question: Why does a run need 333 relations for 192 columns, and can the scan be aimed so it needs fewer?
unit: one batched group addition (Montgomery-shared inversion) on this curve and host

what_is_left.collection: 47.6% of the best run; the relation count is at its floor, so this can now fall only with the column count or the scan constant
what_is_left.selection: 23.4% at 79.5 adds a point, and the algebra it performs is far cheaper than that -- the next thing to measure
what_is_left.table_build: 28.9%; folded_pair_count = |F|^2/(4n) + |F|, one addition per stored pair
